results.title: Deadly bus crash sparks anti-government protests in Iran's Kurdish town
results.description: TEHRAN — Hundreds of people took to the streets of Abdanan in predominantly Kurdish Ilam province in southwestern Iran on Tuesday to protest the deaths of 13 oil and gas workers in a bus crash. The Fars news agency, which is close to the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC), said crowds grew to about 1,000 people in a rare display of anti-government anger that comes against the backdrop of warnings by rights groups of a wartime crackdown on dissent in the country. The bus was carrying employees of the NGL Dehloran oil and gas company when it overturned on the evening of November 14. Thirteen people were killed and 15 were injured. The protesters demanded the resignation of company officials blamed for the accident. Authorities have blamed several parties for the crash. Ilam Province’s traffic police chief cited negligence by the bus driver, the company violating its bus rental contract, and road maintenance failures. Prosecutors have filed charges against the NGL Dehloran CEO and the provincial road maintenance director. Fars reported that after a while the protesters’ chants took on a “political tone.” Online footage showed protesters calling on officials they blamed for the crash to resign. Later videos appeared to show crowds chanting “Death to the dictator,” a slogan aimed at the supreme leader that has become a rallying cry of Iran’s protest movements in the past. Abdanan’s prosecutor, Amrollah Meysaei, warned protesters that the authorities would respond firmly.“Those who seek to exploit this incident to disrupt public order and inflame people’s emotions will be dealt with decisively,” he told the judiciary’s Mizan news agency. It also claimed that some protesters tried to “damage public property.”In January, Iran witnessed some of the largest anti-government protests since the 1979 Islamic Revolution. Security forces shot thousands of protesters in the streets and arrested thousands more. Abdanan — a largely Kurdish town with a population of some 24,000 people — was a hotspot of unrest in January. The Hengaw Organization for Human Rights said at least seven people were detained in Abdanan after Tuesday’s protests — though two were later released. A lawmaker from the province denied there had been any arrests, the Tasnim news agency said on Wednesday. Ten months after the January protests, repression in Iran has intensified, the UN special rapporteur on human rights in Iran said.“There’s been a renewed wave of arrests, resulting in severe sentences, including death sentences,” Mai Sato told the AP in Paris on Wednesday. Sato said that in recent months “at least 39 individuals have been executed” in relation to the January protests, “with at least five carried out in public.”She said authorities have used the war as a cover to continue their suppression of dissent. They have persecuted lawyers who represent dissidents and have broadcast confessions of those accused of wrongdoing on public television, she said.

results.title: North East Delhi riots 2020: Court allows Tahir Hussain to occupy private room for his surgery at RML Hospital
results.description: A Delhi court has allowed the accused in the Delhi riots larger conspiracy case, Tahir Hussain, to occupy a private room at Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital during his admission for surgery scheduled for November 19. The court has also permitted one family member to attend to him at a time, citing security concerns and public attention.
